### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Leber congenital amaurosis 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.780)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10294)

**Proposed mechanism:** RPE65 (HGNC:10294) —DISRUPTS→ Retinal pigment epithelium visual cycle (REACT:R-HSA-198821); Retinal pigment epithelium visual cycle (REACT:R-HSA-198821) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000540); Retinal pigment epithelium visual cycle (REACT:R-HSA-198821) —LEADS_TO→ Impaired dark adaptation (HP:0011234); Retinal pigment epithelium visual cycle (REACT:R-HSA-198821) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital stationary night blindness (HP:0000544); Retinal pigment epithelium visual cycle (REACT:R-HSA-198821) —LEADS_TO→ Reduced visual acuity (HP:0007670). Loss-of-function mutations in RPE65 disrupt the retinal pigment epithelium visual cycle, leading to photoreceptor dysfunction and a spectrum of visual impairments including retinal degeneration, impaired dark adaptation, congenital stationary night blindness, and reduced visual acuity, which are characteristic phenotypes of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in RPE65 that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or the absence of RPE65 involvement in one of the diseases through genetic studies. _(variant: rs12345678 (hypothetical pathogenic variant with >5% frequency in gnomAD))_

**Why it matters:** The shared genetic basis in RPE65 provides a strong foundation for developing targeted gene therapies or other molecular interventions that could potentially treat both diseases simultaneously.

**Proposed mechanism:** RPE65 (HGNC:10294) —DISRUPTS→ Retinal phototransduction cycle (REACT:72734); Retinal phototransduction cycle (REACT:72734) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000547); Retinal phototransduction cycle (REACT:72734) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital stationary night blindness (HP:0000547). Loss-of-function mutations in RPE65 disrupt the retinal phototransduction cycle, leading to retinal degeneration and congenital stationary night blindness.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in RPE65 that lead to a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, the absence of shared variants in gnomAD with an allele frequency > 0.001 would weaken the claim of shared causality. _(variant: HGNC:10294)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism provides a unified therapeutic target for both RPE65-related recessive retinopathy and Leber congenital amaurosis, potentially allowing for gene therapy or other interventions to restore RPE65 function and ameliorate vision loss.

#### 4. nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.466)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2453902)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYO6 (HGNC:7787) —PRODUCES→ Myosin VI (HGNC:7787); Myosin VI (HGNC:7787) —DISRUPTS→ Inner ear hair cell structure and function (GO:0001700); Inner ear hair cell structure and function (GO:0001700) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365); Inner ear hair cell structure and function (GO:0001700) —LEADS_TO→ Vestibular dysfunction (HP:0011340); Myosin VI (HGNC:7787) —DISRUPTS→ Photoreceptor function and maintenance (GO:0001700); Photoreceptor function and maintenance (GO:0001700) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal dystrophy (HP:0012707). Loss-of-function mutations in MYO6 disrupt the function of inner ear hair cells, leading to hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction (Usher syndrome type 1B, Disease A), and also affect photoreceptor integrity, contributing to retinal dystrophies (also part of Disease A). In nonsyndromic hearing loss (Disease B), MYO6 dysfunction specifically impacts hair cell mechanotransduction, resulting solely in hearing impairment.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in MYO6 that leads to gain-of-function or a dominant-negative effect, or a variant present at a high frequency (>1%) in gnomAD in populations affected by nonsyndromic hearing loss but not Usher syndrome type 1B. _(variant: rs373437833)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the MYO6 pathway or its downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both Usher syndrome and nonsyndromic hearing loss, potentially by restoring hair cell function or mitigating photoreceptor degeneration.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CDH23 or PCDH15 in individuals with Usher syndrome or Monk-Spruit syndrome, respectively, with a frequency greater than 1% in large population databases like gnomAD, would challenge the causal link. _(variant: rs143667088)_
